title: Grade 6 Science — Fri, May 29
description: Components of Food — Day 5 of 5: Multi-concept synthesis
subject: science

questions.question: Manu eats only white rice and nothing else. After 3 months, he is pale, tired, and bruises easily. Which nutrients are MOST likely missing?
options: Iron (causing anaemia) and Vitamin C (causing scurvy)
questions.explanation: Rice is mostly starch. Iron deficiency causes anaemia (pale, tired). Vitamin C deficiency causes bleeding/bruising (early scurvy). Both are missing in a rice-only diet.

questions.question: A family in a mountainous area has swollen necks (goitre) despite eating enough food. Their food most likely lacks:
options: Iodine — they may be eating non-iodised salt and foods grown in iodine-poor mountain soil
questions.explanation: Mountain soils are often iodine-poor. Plants grown there lack iodine. Without iodine, thyroid hormones cannot be made → thyroid enlarges → goitre.

questions.question: Sita does the paper spot test on ghee, butter, and rice. Only ghee and butter leave translucent spots. What can she conclude?
options: Ghee and butter contain fat; rice does not contain significant fat
The test only works on dairy products
Translucent spots mean no fat is present
questions.explanation: Translucent greasy spot = fat present. Ghee and butter are high-fat dairy products. Rice is mostly starch with minimal fat. The test correctly identifies the fat-containing foods.

questions.question: A doctor says 'Eat a rainbow of fruits and vegetables'. The SCIENTIFIC reason for this is:
options: Different coloured foods contain different vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants — variety ensures all micronutrients are covered
questions.explanation: Red (lycopene, Vit C), orange/yellow (beta-carotene/Vit A), green (folate, iron, Vit K), purple (anthocyanins) — each colour group represents different nutrients. Variety = complete nutrition.

questions.question: An athlete training 4 hours daily needs _____ more calories than a person with a desk job because:
options: Muscles use ATP (from glucose) during exercise — more physical work = more energy demand = more calories needed
questions.explanation: Calories measure food energy. More physical activity burns more ATP, requiring more glucose (from carbs/fats). An athlete may need 3000-5000 kcal/day vs 2000 for a sedentary person.

questions.question: Why do vegetarians who eat NO animal products need to carefully plan their diet to include B12?
options: B12 is only needed by non-vegetarians
Vitamin B12 is found almost exclusively in animal products — strict vegans can become deficient without supplementation
B12 is in all plant foods
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 (needed for nerve function and blood cells) is NOT found in plant foods. Vegans must get B12 from fortified foods or supplements to prevent deficiency.

questions.question: A community that eats a lot of fish is UNLIKELY to suffer from which deficiency?
options: Iodine deficiency (seafood is rich in iodine)
questions.explanation: Seafood and fish are excellent sources of iodine. Coastal communities that eat lots of fish rarely develop goitre (iodine deficiency).

questions.question: Why does boiling vegetables in a large amount of water and discarding it reduce their nutritional value?
options: Water-soluble vitamins (B and C) leach out into the cooking water — discarding water wastes these vitamins
Vegetable colour is their only nutritional value
questions.explanation: Vitamins B and C are water-soluble — they dissolve into cooking water. Discarding this water throws away vitamins. Steaming or using cooking water (in soup/gravy) retains more nutrition.

questions.question: Obesity (excess body fat) results from eating:
options: Too many calories (especially from fat and refined carbohydrates) compared to calories burned
questions.explanation: When calorie intake consistently exceeds energy expenditure, excess energy is stored as body fat. Obesity is a metabolic imbalance, not just eating one nutrient.

questions.question: A 6-year-old child shows stunted growth, thin muscles, swollen belly. This is MOST likely:
questions.explanation: Stunted growth + muscle wasting + swollen belly (oedema) together point to severe protein-energy malnutrition. Kwashiorkor (protein mainly) or Marasmus (all energy) depending on specifics.

questions.question: In iodine test for starch: you test bread (wheat + starch filler + yeast). Result: strong blue-black. What BEST explains this?
options: Bread is made of wheat flour which is mostly starch — a large amount produces strong blue-black with iodine
questions.explanation: Wheat flour is ~70% starch. Bread (made from flour) is one of the starchiest foods. Strong blue-black colour indicates a large amount of starch.

questions.question: A doctor advises a diabetic patient to eat MORE fibre and LESS refined sugar. The reason is:
options: Fibre slows sugar absorption into blood, preventing blood glucose spikes; refined sugar absorbs instantly, spiking blood glucose dangerously
questions.explanation: Fibre slows digestion and glucose absorption rate, keeping blood sugar stable. Refined sugars spike blood glucose rapidly — dangerous for diabetics who cannot produce enough insulin.

questions.question: Why do breastfed babies grow healthily even though breast milk contains NO iron?
options: Babies are born with enough iron stored in the liver for the first 6 months; breast milk provides everything else
Breast milk tests negative for iron but secretly contains it
Iron in milk is invisible to tests
questions.explanation: Nature plans ahead — foetuses accumulate iron stores in the liver during pregnancy. These stores last ~6 months, by which time solid foods begin. After 6 months, iron-rich foods are needed.

questions.question: If you had to design a single 'perfect food' for a growing 10-year-old, it would need to contain:
options: Carbohydrates + proteins + fats + vitamins + minerals + water + fibre in balanced proportions
questions.explanation: Growing children need: carbs (energy), protein (growth), fat (hormones, brain), vitamins + minerals (body processes), water (all functions), fibre (gut health). No single nutrient can serve all roles.

questions.question: In a village where children eat only white polished rice (not brown rice), many develop beriberi. The solution is:
options: Switching to unpolished (brown) rice or adding B1-rich foods like pulses, nuts, and whole grains
questions.explanation: Polishing removes the rice bran which contains Vitamin B1 (thiamine). Unpolished rice retains B1. Or supplementing with other B1-rich foods (dal, nuts) prevents beriberi.
